summary: Andrew J. Nicholson works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shree Narayan Mishra and held a post at Stony Brook University around 2007.

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University (~1977-1987). He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society (~1989), Executive Director and Resident Scholar at the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (~1993-2015), and senior scholar at the Mind & Life Institute.

Andrew P. Tuck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Princeton University (~-1987) under Victor Preller and Jeffrey Stout, and was also taught by William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, John Pemberton, D. Dennis Hudson, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Alan Sponberg, and Richard Rorty.

Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jay L. Garfield. Between circa 2009 and 2018, he was an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Andrew William Kennedy specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Leeds (~2002-2006) supervised by Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott, with additional instruction from Tony Adam, Jacqui Stewart, Geoffrey Cantor, and Andrew McGonigal.

Andrey Klebanov works in Indology and linguistics. He earned his MA at the University of Hamburg (~2005-2016), supervised by Harunaga Isaacson and Dominic Goodall, alongside numerous other teachers. In 2016, he became a professor at Kyoto University.

Andrey Terentyev (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (circa 1970-1975) and held a post at the Museum of the History of Religion around 1974.

Andries Teeuw (1921-2012) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. After studying at Utrecht University (~1939-1946), he held positions at Utrecht University (1951-1955), the University of Indonesia (~1951-1952), and Leiden University (1955-1986).

Andrzej Gawroński (1885-1927) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Lviv University (~1902-1904) and Leipzig University (~1904-1907), and later held posts at Jagiellonian University (~1912-1916) and Lviv University (~1916-1927).

András Róna-Tas (born 1931) is a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1950-1955), served as President of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (1982), and was a guest lecturer at the University of Vienna (1983-1984).

André Bareau (1921-1993) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Paris, Collège de France, and École Pratique des Hautes Études. His career included posts at the CNRS (1947), EPHE (1956), and Collège de France (1971-1991).

André Couture (born 1945) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1965-1970), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1971-1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1971-1977), later holding a post at Laval University (~1979-2011).

André Padoux (1920-2017) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Paris under Louis Renou and Olivier Lacombe, as well as Lakshman Joo. He was a research director at CNRS (1959) and director of Institut Français Frankfurt (1964).

Andy Rotman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago (~1990-2000) under supervisors Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, joining Smith College in 2000.

Angela Falco Howard specializes in art history, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She completed her doctorate at the Institute of Fine Arts, New York University (~1968-1981) under Alexander Coburn Soper and served as a professor at Rutgers University (~1990-2013).
Angela Manderscheid is a Tibetology scholar. She has held posts as a researcher at the University of Oulu and at the Free University of Berlin.

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Mentored by Nalini Devdas, she earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa (~-2002) and became an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities circa 2002.

Angelo De Gubernatis (1840-1913) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He was a professor at the University of Florence (1863-1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890).

Anil Vidyalankar (born 1928) specializes in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi, and he founded and served as Director of Sandhaan (1988).

Ankur Barua specializes in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong under Dorothy C. Wong, and held a post at the University of Delhi.
